body.statement:
For the corrected positive Fourier minimum-distance construction, under independent environment sampling and \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\),
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}
\Pr_\theta\{D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)>M\rho_N\}=0.
\]
In particular \(D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N)\) uniformly over the model class.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(u_a=dP_\theta^a/d\lambda^n\). The change-of-variables formula, Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:density\text{-}smoothness}\), \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}smoothness}\), and \(\mathrm{ass:decoder\text{-}conditioning}\), and repeated product and chain rules give
\[
c_0K^{-n}\le u_a\le C_0K^n,
\qquad
\|u_a\|_{C^{s_{\mathrm{obs}}}}\le C,
\quad s_{\mathrm{obs}}=k-1.
\]
Only \(k-1\) derivatives are claimed because differentiating the Jacobian of a \(C^k\) decoder consumes one derivative.

Let \(u_{a,L}\) be the orthogonal Fourier projection to \(\|\ell\|_\infty\le L\). Integrating by parts \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}\) times and using orthogonality gives the uniform tail bound
\[
\|u_a-u_{a,L}\|_2^2
\le L^{-2s_{\mathrm{obs}}}
\sum_{j=1}^n\|\partial_j^{s_{\mathrm{obs}}}u_a\|_2^2
\le C L^{-2s_{\mathrm{obs}}}.
\]
For the empirical coefficients, orthogonality and independence give
\[
\mathbb E_\theta\|s_L^a-u_{a,L}\|_2^2
=\sum_{\|\ell\|_\infty\le L}\mathbb E_\theta|\widehat c_{a\ell}-c_{a\ell}|^2
\le C\frac{(2L+1)^n}{N}.
\]
The environment set is finite, so Markov's inequality and a union bound make these estimates simultaneous in \(a\). With \(L=L_N\),
\[
\max_a\|s_L^a-u_a\|_2
=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(L_N^{-s_{\mathrm{obs}}}+\sqrt{L_N^n/N}\right)
=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N).
\]
The same Fourier tail inequality proves the asserted net existence without adding a compactness assumption. For any fixed accuracy \(\delta>0\), choose \(L\) so that the common tail bound is at most \(\delta/4\). The retained Fourier coefficient vectors lie in a bounded finite-dimensional Euclidean ball, which has a finite \(\delta/4\)-net. Hence the finite family of observed densities is totally bounded in \(L^2\). Uniform positivity converts an \(L^2\) net into a Hellinger net. A totally bounded subset admits a finite net whose centers are selected from the subset itself, so choosing one representing model for each selected observed-law family produces \(\mathfrak M_N\subset\mathcal M_{n,k,m}\) at accuracy \(\delta_N\). Adding every common node relabeling preserves finiteness and class membership. Hence the permutation attaining the net distance can be absorbed by selecting the correspondingly relabeled representative.

For all large \(N\), \(u_a\ge c_0K^{-n}>\eta_N\), so the pointwise projection \(s\mapsto\max\{\eta_N,s\}\) cannot increase distance to \(u_a\). Also
\[
\left|\int g_L^a d\lambda^n-1\right|
\le\|g_L^a-u_a\|_1\le\|g_L^a-u_a\|_2.
\]
The corrected normalization and \(\eta_N=o(\rho_N)\) therefore imply
\[
\max_a\|\widehat p_L^a-u_a\|_2=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N).
\]
Since \(u_a\) is uniformly bounded below,
\[
H^2(u_a d\lambda^n,\widehat p_L^a d\lambda^n)
=\frac12\int\frac{(u_a-\widehat p_L^a)^2}{(\sqrt{u_a}+\sqrt{\widehat p_L^a})^2}d\lambda^n
\le C\|u_a-\widehat p_L^a\|_2^2.
\]
Thus the complete-family distance from the true laws to the estimated density family is \(O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N)\), uniformly.

Choose \(\vartheta_N\in\mathfrak M_N\) with \(D_H(\theta,\vartheta_N)\le\delta_N\). The finite-family Hellinger triangle inequality and the defining approximate minimization give
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
&\le D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
 +D_H(\widehat{\mathbb P}_L,\widehat\theta_N)\\
&\le D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)
 +D_H(\widehat{\mathbb P}_L,\vartheta_N)+\delta_N\\
&\le2D_H(\theta,\widehat{\mathbb P}_L)+2\delta_N
=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the notation \(D_H\) against \(\widehat{\mathbb P}_L\) means the same finite Euclidean sum of environment Hellinger distances, with the observed group labels fixed. This proves the uniform law-recovery statement.
